pencereler.0-5: Two jumbo jets collided on a runway in Tenerife. It was the deadliest accident
pencereler.5-12: in aviation history: five hundred eighty three people died. Fog hid the runway, and one jet was still taxiing
pencereler.12-20: on it. The other began its take-off without clearance. A vague radio phrase sounded like permission. Two calls overlapped, and the warning
pencereler.20-30: was lost in noise. No machine failed that day. Aviation radio phrases were standardized afterward.

segmentler.metin: The Tenerife runway collision saw two jumbo jets collide on a foggy runway.
It took only a take-off started without clearance in fog.
So how could a take-off started without clearance in fog do this?
The answer is ambiguous radio phrasing, blocked transmissions and zero visibility on a single runway — and it is why standard radio phrases were enforced and the word take-off reserved for clearance.
